name: targets_list
title: List targets
description: The servers the person made visible to AI clients on this computer (WECOMMANDER → server → AI access). Each has target_id, name, kind (ssh), online, capabilities {exec, read, write, terminal, persistent_tasks, path_policy} and preset (readonly, approval, timed). SSH targets have path_policy "none": a command can reach everything the SSH user can. Pass target to describe one.

name: process_exec
title: Run a command
description: Run a shell command on the target over SSH (no terminal, stdin closed). HIGH risk: unless the target is in a timed autonomous period, the person approves this exact command in the WECOMMANDER app first (the call waits up to 5 minutes). Refused on readonly targets, and sudo/su/doas are refused unless the person allowed sudoers. Output is stdout and stderr interleaved, at most the last 64 KiB, with passwords, keys and tokens masked.

target.description: target_id from targets_list (may be omitted when there is exactly one target).

cwd.description: Folder on the server to run in.

name: fs_list
title: List a folder
description: List a folder on the target over SFTP (at most 1000 entries). "~" or an empty path is the SSH user's home folder.

name: fs_read
title: Read a file
description: Read a file on the target over SFTP as UTF-8 text or base64 (max_bytes default 1 MiB, at most 4 MiB; larger files are refused).

name: fs_stat
title: File information
description: Metadata of a file or folder on the target over SFTP: kind, size, modified time, permissions.

name: server_overview
title: Server overview
description: Linux server overview of the target, read-only: hostname, OS, kernel, uptime, load, CPU %, memory and swap, disks, whether a reboot is required, pending updates, process and zombie counts, and the SSH user's privilege.

name: server_disk_usage
title: Disk usage
description: What fills a Linux disk on the target, read-only: the 40 largest folders directly inside path (default /), sizes in KB, never crossing into another disk, plus Docker's own usage at /.

name: server_processes
title: Server processes
description: Linux processes of the target, read-only: every process (pid, parent, user, state, CPU, memory, run time, command; secrets in command lines masked) and the zombie processes grouped by parent.

name: fs_write
title: Write a file
description: Write base64-encoded bytes (at most 4 MiB) to a file on the target over SFTP, creating it or replacing its content. HIGH risk: the person approves this exact write (path, size, SHA-256) in the WECOMMANDER app first, unless the target is in a timed autonomous period; refused on readonly targets. A path that is a symbolic link is refused (the link is never followed). expected_sha256 refuses the write when the current content changed; create_parents creates missing folders.

expected_sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) the current file must have.

name: fs_mkdir
title: Create a folder
description: Create a folder on the target over SFTP (recursive creates missing parents). Needs the person's approval like other changes; refused on readonly targets.

name: fs_move
title: Move or rename
description: Move or rename a file or folder on the target over SFTP; the destination must not exist. A symbolic link is moved as the link itself. HIGH risk: needs the person's approval; refused on readonly targets.

name: fs_delete
title: Delete
description: Delete a file, link or folder on the target over SFTP. A folder needs recursive (at most 10000 entries; links inside are removed, never followed). The root folder and the SSH user's home folder are refused. expected_sha256 deletes a file only if its content is unchanged. HIGH risk: needs the person's approval; refused on readonly targets.

name: server_cleanup_scan
title: Find what can be cleaned
description: Read-only: what can be safely freed on the Linux target, by category (apt cache, journal older than 7 days, rotated logs, old temp files, crash dumps) and, for every Docker daemon separately (the system one and each user's rootless one, listed in dockers), its build cache and unused images, with the size and the exact command each cleanup runs. Ids of a rootless daemon end in @u<uid>. Use the ids with server_cleanup_run.

name: server_cleanup_run
title: Clean up disk space
description: Frees disk space on the Linux target: runs the fixed cleanup commands of the given categories (ids from server_cleanup_scan) as root (only when the SSH user is root, or the person allowed sudoers and sudo works without a password); a Docker id goes to the daemon it names, through Docker's own prune. Application data, databases, containers and Docker volumes are never touched. HIGH risk: needs the person's approval; refused on readonly targets.

name: server_process_signal
title: Signal a process
description: Sends a signal to one Linux process on the target: action 'reap' asks a parent to collect its zombies (SIGCHLD, harmless), 'term' asks it to stop, 'kill' stops it at once. name must still match the process (a PID reused by another program is refused); the processes that keep the server reachable are refused; a database needs confirm_database. HIGH risk: needs the person's approval; refused on readonly targets.

name: server_timers_list
title: Scheduled tasks
description: Read-only: the target's scheduled tasks: systemd timers (system and the SSH user's own, with schedule, next and last run, the service's command, user and last result) and cron (the user's crontab, /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d and the cron.daily-style folders). Secrets in commands are masked.

name: docker_containers_list
title: Docker containers
description: Read-only: the Docker containers (running and stopped) of every Docker daemon on the target, per daemon: the system one and each user's rootless one (daemon u<uid>). Each container has id (the full 64-hex id), name, image, state, status, created, ports and restart count. A daemon that could not be read carries its error. daemon limits the list to one daemon. At most 500 per daemon.

daemon.description: Docker daemon from docker_containers_list: system (default) or u<uid> for a user's rootless one.

name: docker_container_logs
title: Docker container logs
description: Read-only: the last lines of one Docker container's logs (stdout and stderr merged, timestamped, oldest first). tail 1-2000 (default 200); since limits the window (10m, 1h30m, a Unix time or an RFC 3339 time). At most 256 KiB, newest lines kept; secrets masked.

container.description: Container id or name from docker_containers_list; ref@u<uid> names a rootless daemon.

daemon.description: Docker daemon from docker_containers_list: system (default) or u<uid> for a user's rootless one.

name: docker_container_action
title: Start or stop a container
description: Starts, stops or restarts one Docker container on the target (never removes or prunes anything). The action goes to the full id Docker resolves the reference to, on the daemon it names. WECOMMANDER's own containers are not stopped or restarted. HIGH risk: needs the person's approval; refused on readonly targets.

container.description: Container id or name from docker_containers_list; ref@u<uid> names a rootless daemon.

daemon.description: Docker daemon from docker_containers_list: system (default) or u<uid> for a user's rootless one.
